findings.title: The web job's no-escalation guard catches only one of four ways to write `permissions:`
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by the validator on a sandbox copy: a web job carrying `permissions: write-all` left all 11 guards green, and nothing else in the repo (actionlint included) objected.
findings.scenario: Someone needs the web job to push something — a comment, a baseline, a report. They add one line, `permissions: write-all`, to the job. The job now runs PR-authored browser and build code with a write token. `pnpm run test:tooling` stays green, CI stays green, and the guard whose whole purpose is to stop exactly this says nothing.
findings.whats_wrong: The assertion anchors on end-of-line (`\s*$`), so it only matches the BLOCK form where `permissions:` is alone on its line. YAML has three other spellings and all three bypass it: `permissions: write-all`, `permissions: read-all`, and `permissions: { contents: write }`.
findings.why_it_works: Dropping `\s*$` matches the KEY rather than the whole line, so every spelling trips it. Four-space indentation still uniquely identifies a job-level key in this slice (step list items are six spaces, step keys eight), so the broadened pattern does not start matching comments or steps. The validator confirmed it stays green on today's job, which carries no `permissions:` key at all — so the fix is non-breaking.
findings.extras: The same reviewers named two adjacent narrownesses worth folding into one edit: the no-secrets assertion `/\$\{\{\s*secrets\./` is case-sensitive while GitHub Actions expression contexts are not (`${{ SECRETS.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` passes — add `/i`), and a job-level `secrets:` key is unchecked.
findings.spike: The validator built the mutation and ran the suite. Not yet applied.

findings.title: The new `@source not '../e2e/**'` line has no test gate, and its sibling does
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by the validator: a repo-wide grep finds the only `@source not` text gate is tooling/assert-design-system-css.test.mjs:121, which pins `../scripts/**` only. No test, script or CI step asserts the new `../e2e/**` line.
findings.scenario: Months from now someone tidies web/app/globals.css and deletes the `@source not '../e2e/**';` line, because on a healthy build removing it changes nothing you can see. Tailwind resumes scanning web/e2e/. The comments in those test files mention `bg-rail`, `hover:bg-elevate`, `bg-muted`, `bg-popover`, `text-destructive` and `h-11` — so Tailwind now GENERATES those utilities from prose. The NH-315 stylesheet canary, whose job is to fail when a scanned-only utility goes missing from the emitted CSS, now finds them present no matter what the app does. Everything stays green over a broken build.
findings.whats_wrong: This PR adds a second standing fence to Tailwind's source scanning and AGENTS.md now says 'Do not remove either line' — but only the first line is mechanically enforced. The file that enforces it, tooling/assert-design-system-css.test.mjs, is not in this PR.
findings.why_it_works: The test already owns the sibling line and already runs in the `quality` job through `pnpm run test:tooling`, so this is four lines in a file that is already wired up. The pattern must be a LITERAL regex, not one built from a variable — this repo's `sast` hook blocks `javascript.lang.security.audit.detect-non-literal-regexp`, which is deviation #3 in the PR body.
findings.extras: The learnings reviewer measured the hazard's current reach honestly: today 0 of the canary's ten REQUIRED_SELECTORS appear under web/e2e, so the PR's 'all 10 still present' check is a no-regression result rather than proof the line is load-bearing. The risk is forward-looking — the next selector added to the canary could be one web/e2e discusses in prose.
findings.spike: Validator reproduced the absence of any gate. The fix itself is untested (nobody added the assertion and ran the suite).

findings.title: The `player-skeleton` baseline is a picture of a blank white page; the Skeleton is painted over
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by the validator, independently of both reviewers, by decoding the committed PNG: the notation box region (x 96-1279, y 73-819) is 884,448 pure-white pixels with ZERO non-white pixels. The Skeleton paints --skeleton #888; the only (136,136,136) pixels anywhere in the image are the 6 px header loading strip at y 58-63 — which proves the token renders fine when it is not occluded.
findings.scenario: You open web/e2e/pages.vr.ts-snapshots/player-skeleton-chromium-linux.png expecting to see the first-visit loading Skeleton — the shot is named for it, and the PR says all ten baselines were opened and looked at. What is actually in the file is a blank white rectangle. If someone deletes the Skeleton component outright, this shot still passes: it is already photographing its absence.
findings.whats_wrong: web/app/play/NotationSurface.tsx renders the absolutely-positioned Skeleton (`absolute inset-0`, no z-index) BEFORE an opaque sibling carrying `isolate ... bg-white`. `isolation: isolate` makes that sibling a stacking context, and as a non-positioned stacking context it paints later in tree order — on top. So the Skeleton is covered. The shot's guard against this is `toBeVisible()`, which checks the bounding box and CSS visibility and has no concept of occlusion, so it passes on a fully hidden element.
findings.why_it_works: `elementFromPoint` returns whatever actually paints at that coordinate, so the assertion fails exactly when something covers the Skeleton — which is the state the committed baseline is in today. That is the point: adding it turns a silent pass into a red test that names the real problem. THE DECISION this needs is what to do next, and it is a product call rather than a test call: (a) treat the occlusion as a bug, raise the Skeleton above the viewport in NotationSurface.tsx (the only other z-10 sibling is the engine-error banner, which is mutually exclusive with the Skeleton because the Skeleton is gated on `!failure`), then regenerate the baseline — or (b) treat the white page as the intended first-visit render, and rename the shot and its comments so they stop claiming to cover the Skeleton.
findings.extras: The occlusion itself is pre-existing product behaviour, not something this diff introduced: `isolate` arrived with PR #176 on 2026-09-27, the Skeleton with #159 on 2026-09-20. What this diff adds is a baseline and an assertion that cannot see the problem. The learnings reviewer links it to two recorded lessons: 'baselines freeze whatever renders' (feedback_render_ui_before_accepting) and the toBeVisible/opacity trap (playwright_tobevisible_opacity_zero) — this is the occlusion sibling of the second.
findings.spike: Measured three ways: the testing reviewer, the learnings reviewer (882,087 of ~890k px white, plus a real-Chrome reproduction using the real class strings), and the validator (884,448 px, zero non-white). The suggested assertion is untested as code.

findings.title: The merge-gate guard does not stop `continue-on-error`, and a skipped web job counts as a pass
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by the validator on a sandbox copy: adding `continue-on-error: true` above the web browser-lane step AND replacing the job's `if:` with `${{ false }}` left all 11 guards green. It also found the aggravating fact — ci.yml's ci-green allow-list explicitly accepts `skipped`.
findings.scenario: The web job goes red on something nobody wants to debug today. Someone adds `continue-on-error: true` to the step, or narrows the job's `if:` so it stops running. The ten pixel shots are now decorative: the job reports success (or skips, which ci-green accepts), `CI Green` goes green, and the merge-blocking gate this entire PR exists to build is a no-op. Every guard still passes.
findings.whats_wrong: The guard asserts the job is REGISTERED in ci-green's needs (`/^\s+web,$/m`) but never that it can actually fail the build. Registration and enforcement are different properties, and only the first is checked.
findings.why_it_works: The first assertion closes the 'cannot fail' route; the second pins the exact condition under which the job runs, so narrowing it is a visible edit rather than a silent one. Stripping comment lines first matters because the slice includes comments, and the `vr-report` job legitimately uses `continue-on-error` — which is why the check must stay scoped to the web slice rather than the whole workflow.
findings.spike: Both mutations built and run by the validator. The fix is untested as written.

findings.title: The one-invocation guard counts `run:` lines, so a second Playwright run inside a `run: |` block is invisible
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by the validator: a second step whose `run: |` block calls `pnpm exec playwright test --project=chromium` plus `playwright install chromium` on continuation lines left the count at 1 and the `playwright install` check unfired — all 11 guards green. `run: |` is already this workflow's own idiom (ci.yml lines 125, 194, 276, 574).
findings.scenario: Someone splits the lane back into two invocations for a reason that looks good at the time, writing the second one inside a `run: |` block. The whole point of this PR's single unscoped invocation — one `next build` serving behaviour, axe and pixels — is gone, the job builds twice, and the guard that exists to catch a second invocation reports exactly one.
findings.whats_wrong: The regex anchors each match to a line that begins with `run:`. A YAML block scalar puts the actual commands on CONTINUATION lines, which never start with `run:`, so they are not counted. The adjacent `playwright install` check at lines 108-112 has the identical blind spot.
findings.why_it_works: Dropping the `run:` anchor counts the command wherever it appears, including inside a block scalar. Stripping comment lines first prevents a comment that mentions `playwright test` from inflating the count. Apply the same stripping to the `playwright install` assertion, which fails the same way.
findings.spike: Validator built the `run: |` mutation and confirmed the bypass. Fix untested.

findings.title: Nothing stops a screenshot tolerance that makes all ten shots pass on any pixels
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by the validator: sandbox copies with `expect: { toHaveScreenshot: { maxDiffPixelRatio: 1 } }` in web/playwright.e2e.config.ts, and with `maxDiffPixels: 1_000_000` on the landing shot, both left all 11 guards green. Both are real Playwright options, and no ESLint rule or semgrep config in this repo bans them.
findings.scenario: The pixel lane goes red on a diff someone judges cosmetic. The fastest way to green is one option: `maxDiffPixelRatio: 1` in the config, or `maxDiffPixels` on the offending shot. All ten shots now pass against any rendering whatsoever. The lane still runs, still reports ten passing tests, and every guard is green — including the one that checks the lane has shots to run.
findings.whats_wrong: pages.vr.ts:29 states a policy — no comparison options, default threshold only — and that policy has no mechanism. This is the shortest path from a working gate to a decorative one: one line, in a file the guards already read.
findings.before:
// the shot/baseline guard reads the sources but never looks at comparison options
const shots = [...source.matchAll(/toHaveScreenshot\('([^']+\.png)'/g)].map((match) => ...);
findings.why_it_works: It closes the one-line disarm directly. One implementation detail the reviewer measured: strip only `//` line comments from web/playwright.e2e.config.ts (`.replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, '')`), NOT with the file's existing `stripComments` helper — that helper treats the `'**/*.e2e.ts'` glob as the start of a block comment and swallows the code after it.
findings.extras: This is the only finding in the set from a single reviewer that I kept at P2 rather than demoting to a residual risk, which is the default for a single-source reliability P2 with no current defect. I kept it because it names the shortest existing path to silently disarming all ten shots at once, and because the validator reproduced it. Flagging the single source so you can weigh it.
findings.spike: Two mutations built and run by the validator. Fix untested.

findings.title: The shot/baseline guard lists `web/e2e` one level deep, while Playwright collects `**/*.vr.ts` recursively
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by the validator: a nested web/e2e/player/nested.vr.ts that was test.skip-ped, omitted failOnUnexpectedPageErrors() and carried an orphan baseline in its own -snapshots folder left all 11 guards green. It also confirmed `**/*.vr.ts` really is recursive in this repo — client/playwright.config.ts discovers client/src/components/ui/**/*.vr.ts that way.
findings.scenario: Someone adds shots in a subfolder — web/e2e/player/transport.vr.ts — because ten shots in one file is getting long. Playwright runs them. None of the guard's protections apply to them: they can be skipped, they can omit the page-error hook, and their baselines live in a folder the guard never opens.
findings.whats_wrong: `readdirSync(dir)` is non-recursive, and line 343 reads ONE hard-coded snapshot folder (web/e2e/pages.vr.ts-snapshots/). Playwright's default snapshot template embeds {testFileDir}, so a nested shot's baselines land outside the folder the guard inspects.
findings.why_it_works: It makes the guard's discovery match the config's. Pair it with building baselineNames by unioning each shot file's own `<shot>-snapshots/` folder (treating ENOENT as empty) instead of hard-coding one path — so a shot with no baseline folder at all still trips the existing set-equality assertion rather than being skipped.
findings.spike: Validator created the nested file and confirmed every protection was bypassed. Fix untested.

findings.title: Five documents state the gate has ten shots and no test holds that number
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by the validator: appending an eleventh toHaveScreenshot plus its -chromium-linux baseline to sandbox copies left all 11 guards green. Meanwhile AGENTS.md:193, web/README.md:22, docs/runbooks/vr-a11y-testing.md:13 and pages.vr.ts:23/89/342 all say ten.
findings.scenario: The two deferred popover shots get added. Nothing fails, so nobody updates the prose. AGENTS.md, both READMEs, the runbook and three code comments now all say 'ten' about a twelve-shot gate, and the comment at pages.vr.ts:24 — 'an eleventh should have to justify itself' — has no way to make anyone justify anything.
findings.whats_wrong: The guard pairs shots with baselines by set equality, which is the right check for a MISSING baseline but says nothing about the count. The file already uses the hard-number idiom one screen up: `const EXPECTED_PLAYWRIGHT_PINS = 3;` at line 206.
findings.before:
const EXPECTED_PLAYWRIGHT_PINS = 3;
// ...no equivalent for the shot count
findings.why_it_works: It mirrors the file's own existing convention, and it forces the prose edit to happen in the same commit as the eleventh shot, because the test names the documents that disagree.
findings.spike: Validator added an eleventh shot and baseline, confirmed green. Fix untested.

findings.title: The spec now says `Status: Implemented` while its body describes a different gate
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by direct grep: the spec says `Status: Implemented`, contains 18 occurrences of 'nine', 5 lines naming the removed `test:vr:docker` script, and line 391's 'Candidates deliberately **not** in v1' heading — under which the drag-over state sits as shot number ten.
findings.scenario: An agent is pointed at this spec by ci.yml:424 and by pages.vr.ts:55-63. It reads 'Status: Implemented' and trusts the body. The body tells it there are nine shots (there are ten), that the drag-over overlay is deliberately not in v1 (it is shot ten), that the timeout is 120_000 (it is 180_000), that the toast ceiling is 10 s (it is 15 s), that the script is `test:vr:docker` (renamed), and it shows three assertion snippets the shipped code explicitly rejected as vacuous.
findings.whats_wrong: Only the Status line was edited. None of this drift is among the eight deviations the PR body declares, so the PR presents the spec as matching what shipped.
findings.before: Status: Implemented. v0 Plan C (the Settings and Tracks popovers) has merged, and its ...
findings.after:
Status: Implemented, with deltas — see **Shipped deltas** below.

## Shipped deltas

This spec is kept as the design record. What shipped differs as follows:

- **Ten shots, not nine.** The drag-over overlay (listed under 'Candidates deliberately not in v1')
  shipped as the tenth.
- **`timeout: 180_000`,** not 120_000 — a 120 s project cap pre-empts the expect ceilings.
- **A 15 s toast ceiling,** not 10 s.
- **`test:client:docker*` / `test:web:docker*`,** not `test:vr:docker*`.
- **Three assertion snippets here are superseded** — the shipped versions reject them as unable to fail.
- **Measured heights are 113 / 627 / 576 px,** not 576 / 852 / 576.
findings.why_it_works: A banner under the Status line is this repo's established convention for a superseded document, and it keeps the archive readable rather than rewriting history — which matters here because the maintainer re-reads archived documents when revisiting a decision. The alternative, editing all 18 'nine's and 5 script names in place, is more churn and loses the design record. Either way the omission belongs in the PR's declared deviations.
findings.spike: Grep-verified counts. The banner text above is a draft, not applied.

findings.title: Two of the four surface assertions pass for any opaque colour that is not the page background
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by reading the helper, and measured by the testing reviewer against the real build: rail rgb(244,246,249) and transport-row rgb(251,252,254) versus body lab(100 0 0) return true; transparent, --background and --card return false (the NH-315 failure class they target); but swaps to --muted, --elevate and --panel ALSO return true.
findings.scenario: Someone swaps the rail's background from `bg-rail` to `bg-muted`. The pixel difference scores 20 against Playwright's 1408.6 cutoff, so the screenshot cannot see it. The computed-colour assertion that exists precisely to catch what the screenshot cannot see also passes, because `bg-muted` is opaque and is not the body colour. The change ships unnoticed.
findings.whats_wrong: `surfaceDiffersFromPageBackground` asserts a DIFFERENCE, not an identity. The other two surface assertions in this same file do it the stronger way: they resolve the expected token through a throwaway probe and assert equality (`.toBe(elevate)`, `.toBe(expectedTint)`). These two do not.
findings.why_it_works: Probe and element then come back through the same serializer, so equality is meaningful — the testing reviewer checked that these hex tokens do read back equal on the real build. The `not.toBe('rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)')` precheck keeps a deleted token from making the comparison vacuous, which is the same guard the existing --elevate assertion uses. If you apply this, update the two matching entries in the guard's `surfaceAnchors` to `var(--rail)` and `var(--panel)` and keep the count at four.
findings.spike: Behaviour measured against the real build by the testing reviewer. The replacement helper is untested.

findings.title: The new `web` job inlines the pnpm and Node setup that AGENTS.md says to use the composite for
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by grep: AGENTS.md:132 states the rule; the `web` job contains zero references to `setup-js`. The pre-existing `vr` job does the same thing, with a comment explaining why.
findings.scenario: The next person authoring a CI job reads the AGENTS.md rule — 'use `- uses: ./.github/actions/setup-js` AFTER actions/checkout@v6; do not inline the pnpm/node setup' — notices two container jobs ignoring it, and cannot tell whether that is an exception or a mistake. The rule has one documented exception, dependency-free Node scripts, and this is not it.
findings.whats_wrong: `run: corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` inside the new job, with no setup-js step. The `vr` job already does this, so the rule now has two undocumented exceptions rather than one.

findings.title: The shot named 'long enough to scroll' runs at a viewport where the score does not scroll
findings.verified: DERIVED, not re-measured. The shot has no test.use override, so it runs at the chromium project's 1280x900. The author's own deviation #2 measured Punk.gp's notation at 627 px against a 576 px box — at the behaviour lane's 720 px viewport. At 900 px the box grows by the same 180 px to about 756 px, which is larger than 627 px, so nothing overflows.
findings.scenario: You look at player-long-score-chromium-linux.png to check the scroll affordance on a long score. The notation fits the box, so there is nothing to scroll and no affordance in the picture. The shot's title, the runbook's shot list and the spec all say this shot covers a score long enough to scroll.
findings.whats_wrong: Deviation #2 in the PR body corrects the plan's height measurement and concludes the box overflows — but that measurement is from the 720 px-tall behaviour lane, while the pixel lane runs at 900 px tall. The conclusion does not transfer to the viewport this shot actually uses.
findings.why_it_works: At 1280x720 the box is the 576 px one the measurement describes and 627 px of notation overflows it, so the picture contains the thing the title claims. Regenerate with `pnpm test:web:docker:update` afterwards. If the shot was only ever meant to prove a second score loads, the cheaper fix is to rename it and drop the 'long enough to scroll' claim from the title, the runbook shot list and the spec — which is a smaller change but gives up the pixel coverage.
findings.spike: Not re-rendered at either viewport. The 627/576 px figures are the author's; the viewport difference is read from the config. Verify by rendering before choosing.

findings.title: `web/README.md` and `web/AGENTS.md` both describe `test:e2e` as the web job's script
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by grep: web/README.md:20 says `test:e2e` is 'what the `web` CI job runs'; web/AGENTS.md:17 says 'The Playwright script is `test:e2e`' (singular). The job runs an unscoped superset of both projects, and this PR's own guard forbids naming `test:e2e` in that job.
findings.scenario: A red `web` job sends someone to web/README.md to find what to run locally. They run `test:e2e`, it passes, and they conclude CI is wrong — because the failure was in `test:vr`, which the job also runs and the README does not mention.
findings.whats_wrong: Two statements made stale by this PR: the job now runs one unscoped `playwright test` covering both the `e2e` and `chromium` projects, and web/ now has four Playwright scripts rather than one.
findings.before:
<!-- web/README.md:20 -->
| `pnpm --filter @notation-hero/web run test:e2e` | Behaviour + accessibility against the built app — what the `web` CI job runs |

<!-- web/AGENTS.md:17 -->
- The Playwright script is `test:e2e`, never `test`: the `quality` CI job runs `pnpm -r run test`
findings.after:
<!-- web/README.md:20 -->
| `pnpm --filter @notation-hero/web run test:e2e` | Behaviour + accessibility project only. The `web` CI job runs it together with `test:vr` in ONE unscoped `playwright test`, so a red CI run can be a `test:vr` failure. |

<!-- web/AGENTS.md:17 -->
- The Playwright scripts are `test:e2e` (behaviour + axe) and `test:vr` / `test:vr:update` (the ten
  shots), each scoped with `--project`; never name one `test`: the `quality` CI job runs
  `pnpm -r run test` with no browsers installed.
findings.why_it_works: It names both lanes and keeps web/AGENTS.md's prohibition intact, so the next reader can map a red job to the right local command.

findings.title: A surface anchor still matches after the comparison it guards is deleted, if the probe line stays
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by reading, but NARROWED on verification. The guard also carries a count assertion (surfaceAssertions.length === surfaceAnchors.length) and its comment says that count is what makes dropping one impossible. The count is right about the realistic case; the bypass needs someone to delete the expect and leave a now-pointless probe line behind.
findings.scenario: Someone deletes the `.toBe(elevate)` comparison from the ghost-hover shot but leaves `probe.style.backgroundColor = 'var(--elevate)'` above it. The anchor searches for `var(--elevate)`, finds it on the probe line, and passes. The count stays at four. The assertion is gone and the guard is green.
findings.whats_wrong: Two of the four anchors match the PROBE's CSS expression rather than the comparison. The probe can outlive the assertion it feeds.
findings.why_it_works: The pattern then fails when the assertion is removed, which is the state the anchor exists to detect. Keep the probe shapes in `surfaceAssertions` so the count assertion is unchanged. If you apply C-11, the first two patterns change shape with it — do C-11 first.

findings.title: A new comment narrates the pre-change state and cites a ticket id
findings.verified: CONFIRMED by grep, and SCOPED on verification: `(NH-320)` appears twice in added lines. Line 386 narrates history. Line 424 is `# Spec: docs/specs/2026-09-21-web-visual-regression-gate.md (NH-320).` — a document pointer, which is a legitimate reference rather than a task-number-as-explanation. Only 386 is the violation.
findings.scenario: Someone reads ci.yml in two years. The comment tells them the lane 'moved' to the web job under a ticket number they cannot look up from the file, and describes a state that no longer exists, instead of telling them what the job does now.
findings.whats_wrong: This repo's convention is that code comments name the thing so they read correctly in ten years, while prose, plans and tables keep the ticket numbers. A past-tense 'moved (NH-320)' is both the narration and the id.
findings.before: # MSW. web/'s browser lane moved to the `web` job (NH-320), which runs it in the Playwright
findings.after:
# MSW. web/'s browser lane lives in the `web` job, which runs it in the Playwright container so
# one `next build` serves behaviour, axe and pixels together.
findings.why_it_works: Present tense describes what is true, and it stays true. The same reviewer noted tooling/docker-playwright.sh lines 12-15 narrate the pre-change state too ('the inlined form had already reached ~400 characters each'); that is a measured justification rather than a ticket id, so it is weaker, but it could shorten to 'One helper for client/ and web/, so the volume list and the image pin live in one place.' The nine older NH- citations elsewhere in ci.yml are out of scope — they predate this diff.

findings.title: AGENTS.md asks for a calculation it does not provide where an agent reads it
findings.verified: CONFIRMED but CORRECTED. The reviewer said the formula exists only in docs/plans. Grep shows it is also in web/e2e/pages.vr.ts and in the spec. It is absent from AGENTS.md and from docs/runbooks/vr-a11y-testing.md — the two documents that give the instruction.
findings.scenario: An agent adds a low-contrast surface to /play. AGENTS.md tells it to 'score its step against that same cutoff first' and the runbook repeats the instruction. Neither says how. The likely outcome is skipping the computed-background assertion and trusting the screenshot — which is the exact failure the caveat exists to prevent, because a surface change at a delta of 5 or 20 is invisible to the comparison.
findings.whats_wrong: An instruction whose method lives somewhere the reader was not sent. Because the formula does exist in pages.vr.ts and in the spec, the fix is a cross-reference rather than new authorship.
findings.before:
<!-- AGENTS.md:193 and docs/runbooks/vr-a11y-testing.md:50 -->
... needs its own computed `background-color` assertion beside the shot, not a baseline alone
... score its step against that same cutoff first
findings.after:
<!-- add the method beside the instruction, in the runbook -->
Score the step first: Playwright's per-pixel distance is
`0.5053*dY^2 + 0.299*dI^2 + 0.1957*dQ^2` in YIQ, compared against `35215 * threshold^2`
(1408.6 at the default 0.2 threshold). The worked version, with this design system's measured
steps, is in the `surfaceDiffersFromPageBackground` comment in `web/e2e/pages.vr.ts`.
Above the cutoff the picture already covers it; under it, add the assertion.
findings.why_it_works: It makes the instruction executable at the point of use and points at the existing worked example instead of duplicating it. A small tooling/ script taking two colours and printing the verdict would be stronger still; the cross-reference is the cheap version.
findings.extras: The same reviewer recomputed this design system's step scores independently and got 5.3, 19.6, 80.7 and 171 against the documented 5, 20, 80 and 173 — close enough that no conclusion changes. It also flagged that the spec's line 315-316 attributes a score of 20 to rail-against-page-background where the correct pair is rail-against-panel (rail against the white page is about 45); the code comment at pages.vr.ts:113 has it right.

dropped_findings.title: Only client/README documents that a client/ visual change also moves web/'s baselines
dropped_findings.drop_reason: Verified and rejected. client/README.md:164 documents it in full, including the trap and the remedy: 'A `client/` visual change also moves `web/`'s ten page baselines ... and the `web` job is gated on the `code` filter — so a `client/`-only PR runs it. Regenerate them with `pnpm test:web:docker:update` and commit them in the same PR.' That is the document a client/ contributor reads when making a client/ visual change, so the placement is right. AGENTS.md and the runbook being silent is a mild redundancy gap, not a defect. Moved to residual risks.

dropped_findings.title: pressEveryTransportToggle breaks player-states.ts's stated no-waits contract
dropped_findings.drop_reason: Verified and rejected. The function's own docstring states and justifies the exception: 'The `toBeEnabled` wait is part of REACHING this state, not of settling it: the clicks cannot happen before the engine and the soundfont are up.' The module header's rule is about SETTLING waits. The author anticipated the objection and documented it at the call site, which is the false-positive category 'code that looks wrong but is intentional — check comments for evidence of intent'. Moved to residual risks.

dropped_findings.title: A missing baseline would be written and pass (toHaveScreenshot updateSnapshots: 'missing')
dropped_findings.drop_reason: My own fast-pass candidate, disproved by the adversarial reviewer reading the vendor source. Playwright 1.61.1's handleMissing returns pass:true but attaches a softError, which worker/workerProcessEntry.js:1050-1052 turns into _failWithError. A new or renamed shot therefore CANNOT write its own baseline and pass. Withdrawn.

dropped_findings.title: route.continue() after test teardown leaves an unhandled rejection
dropped_findings.drop_reason: My own fast-pass candidate, disproved by the reliability reviewer by measurement: a stall timer firing after the test ended resolves silently through Playwright's LongStandingScope.safeRace and never reaches workerMain.unhandledError; context close with a never-handled route takes 1-3 ms. Withdrawn.

dropped_findings.title: Four maintainability refactor proposals
dropped_findings.drop_reason: Demoted to residual risks per the review protocol's rule for single-reviewer maintainability findings with no violated contract and no current defect: re-implementing the VR-lane guard on `playwright test --list` instead of regexes; moving the drag/tooltip/stall helpers into player-states.ts; extracting the duplicated computed-background probe; and sharing the job-slicing and file-read idioms across the guard file. All are reasonable and none is a defect. Full text in the reviewer artifact.

triage_groups.title: Guards a one-line edit can walk past
triage_groups.context: Seven separate bypasses of tooling/workflow-guards.test.mjs, every one reproduced on a sandbox copy that left all 11 guards green. They share one file and one root cause: the guards match text shapes rather than the properties they mean to pin.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: One commit to tooling/workflow-guards.test.mjs. Do #1 and #4 first — they are the two that let the gate become a no-op (a write token, and a job that cannot fail or does not run). Then #5, #6, #7, #8. Do #16 after #11, because #11 changes the shape its first two patterns match.
triage_groups.why: Each fix is a few lines in a file that already runs in CI, and the file already uses the needed idioms (EXPECTED_PLAYWRIGHT_PINS for a pinned count, comment stripping for slices).

triage_groups.title: The fence around the gate has no fence
triage_groups.context: The new Tailwind scan exclusion is the thing that keeps test-file prose from manufacturing CSS and blinding the NH-315 canary. Its sibling line is pinned by a test; this one is not.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Four lines in tooling/assert-design-system-css.test.mjs, which already pins the sibling. Use a literal regex — this repo's sast hook blocks one built from a variable.
triage_groups.why: Highest ratio of consequence to effort in the set, and the file is already wired into the quality job.

triage_groups.title: Two shots do not photograph what their titles claim
triage_groups.context: player-skeleton's committed baseline is 884,448 pure-white pixels with zero non-white — the Skeleton is painted over by a later sibling with `isolation: isolate`, and toBeVisible() cannot see occlusion. player-long-score runs at a viewport where the notation fits, so nothing scrolls.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Decide each one's intent before touching code. #3: fix the stacking in NotationSurface.tsx and re-baseline, or rename the shot. #14: scope the shot to 1280x720 and re-baseline, or rename it. Both need `pnpm test:web:docker:update` afterwards.
triage_groups.why: Neither is a test bug you can just fix — each turns on what the shot is FOR, and #3's first option changes product rendering.

triage_groups.title: An assertion weaker than it reads
triage_groups.context: Two of the four surface assertions assert a difference rather than an identity, so a swap between two neutral surfaces passes both the screenshot and the assertion written to catch what the screenshot cannot see.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Replace surfaceDiffersFromPageBackground with the probe-and-equality helper the same file already uses twice, then update the two matching guard anchors (which is #16).
triage_groups.why: The stronger form already exists in this file; this makes all four consistent.

triage_groups.title: The documents describe a gate that did not ship
triage_groups.kind: mixed — #10 is a decision-gate, the rest apply-queue
triage_groups.context: The spec says Implemented while its body describes nine shots, a 120 s timeout and renamed scripts; the changelog records none of the four execution-time decisions; the digest is pasted into two unguarded documents; both web/ documents call test:e2e the job's script; one comment narrates history with a ticket id; and AGENTS.md asks for a calculation it does not provide.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Do #9 first — it is the largest divergence and the document CI points agents at. #10 is yours to ratify, not an agent's to write. #12, #15, #17 and #18 are small prose edits that can go in one commit.
triage_groups.why: These are what a future agent reads and trusts. A premature `Status: Implemented` is more dangerous than a missing document.

triage_groups.title: A CI convention with two undocumented exceptions
triage_groups.context: AGENTS.md says a new CI job must use the setup-js composite. The vr job already inlines the install, and now web does too.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Rule it: document the container-job exception in AGENTS.md, or rewrite both jobs to use the composite and prove the baselines still render.
triage_groups.why: Only you can decide whether the rule or the practice is wrong.

pre_existing_findings.title: The engine module import has no timeout, so a stalled load swallows a file pick silently
pre_existing_findings.scenario: Your network stalls the vendored alphaTab module — it never resolves and never rejects. You pick a file. Nothing happens: no notation, no error panel, no toast. The pick is simply gone, and the app waits forever.
pre_existing_findings.whats_wrong: loadAlphaTabEngine awaits a dynamic import with no timer, and the result is memoised as `pending`. Every other hang in this area has a backstop — NotationSurface.tsx:125 has a 60 s music-font timeout — this one does not.
pre_existing_findings.proposed_fix: Race the import against a 60 s rejecting timer and clear it in a finally. About ten lines, no dependency. `pending` then caches the rejection exactly as it does for a failed import, so AlphaTabEngineProvider shows the existing engine-error panel and runRequestNotation's .catch raises the E205 toast and releases openInFlight — no new code paths. Keep the ceiling above ~30 s so the pixel lane's Infinity-stall Skeleton shot is unaffected.
pre_existing_findings.why_pre_existing: The file is not in this diff and the gate does not depend on this for correctness — the shots pass either way. This PR is how it was FOUND: the two deliberately-broken-engine shots exercise the stalled-load path for the first time. Worth a ticket rather than this PR.
pre_existing_findings.why_it_matters: A silent swallow is the worst failure shape for a file-open: the person cannot tell whether they clicked wrong, the file is bad, or the app is broken.

residual_risks_and_testing_gaps_pointer: 60 residual risks and 23 testing gaps were collected across the ten reviewers and are NOT repeated here. They live in the per-reviewer artifacts under /tmp/compound-engineering-501/ce-code-review/20261002-151735-0721868c/ (*.json for the eight structured reviewers, agent-native.md and learnings.md for the two prose ones). The five most load-bearing, in case triage wants them: (1) the chromium project can be silenced with testIgnore/grep/grepInvert and every guard stays green; (2) the pin guard proves the three homes AGREE on a digest, never that the digest is the one the baselines were rendered by, and v1.61.1-noble is a re-pushable tag; (3) retries: 2 means a flaky-then-passed shot exits 0 with no failOnFlakyTests, and determinism evidence covers only 2 of the 10 shots; (4) the three ways to run this lane differ silently — the docker helper passes no CI, so it runs only --project=chromium with retries 0; (5) the PR body's 'read a red web job as a possible consequence of the container move' paragraph is now STALE — the web job has passed twice on these baselines (102 passed, 0 flaky, one next build), which also retires the spec's cross-architecture concern since arm64-generated baselines matched the x64 runner.
